bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's flood risk is changing, not just repeating | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: October 03, 2026 Bihar’s flood risk is changing, not just repeating Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Eklavya Prasad Bihar’s flood story is both familiar and evolving. While many communities face recurring inundation, erosion and infrastructure damage, changing flood patterns are pushing the geography of risk into new settlements, exposing more households to river floods, embankment breaches, flash floods and prolonged waterlogging Every year, Bihar counts its floods. Districts affected. Gram Panchayats affected. People evacuated. Relief camps, boats, damaged houses, families receiving gratuitous relief. These numbers matter; they let the state mobilise quickly. But after three consecutive years of flood figures, a harder question is becoming difficult to avoid: what does Bihar learn from one flood before the next arrives? The Disaster Management Department’s reports offer a starting point. On October 15, 2024, it recorded 28 affected districts, 979 Gram Panchayats and 52.46 lakh people. On October 15, 2025, the figures stood at 23 districts, 600 Gram Panchayats and 48 lakh people. The September 24, 2026 report shows 15 districts, 576 Gram Panchayats and 50.49 lakh people, a total likely to rise after the recent flooding along the Gandak. These are snapshots from different stages of different floods, so they do not measure severity. Yet the pattern is striking. The reported geography of impact has shifted considerably, while the number of people affected stays in a similar range. What changed because of what Bihar experienced the year before? Vulnerability in Bihar is neither wholly repetitive nor wholly new. Some embankments, settlements, roads and households face recurring exposure and accumulating loss. Elsewhere, a river shifts course, a breach redirects water, or a flash flood reaches people never considered at high risk. A single breach is an event; repeated breaches near the same spot signal persistent vulnerability, demanding a different response from a newly affected area. And when a flood behaves unexpectedly, that should reshape the state’s understanding of risk. Every flood produces information. Breaches are reported, roads cut, crops lost. Engineers inspect embankments; communities know where water entered and where it stagnated. When the water recedes, what happens to all this knowledge? Does a repeatedly flooded location acquire a risk profile? Does a newly affected area prompt a revision of vulnerability maps? Does a known breach or drainage failure shape how infrastructure is designed and maintained before the next monsoon? Bihar’s machinery for emergency response is extensive. What is harder to see is a learning loop connecting one year’s experience to the next year’s decisions. A response system asks: what must we do now? A learning system asks: why did this happen here, what did we learn, what must change, and who will make sure it does before it happens again? The first is indispensable during a flood. The second decides whether the state can move from recurring emergency management towards sustained risk reduction. Once the emergency passes, the questions should change. Why did the breach occur? national_raw_news.title: Indian Archer Kumkum Mohod clinches gold in recurve event in Asian Games 6 hours ago 129
national_raw_news.content: The gold rush continued for India at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Indian athletes delivered a stellar performance on Day 14, clinching 17 gold medals in Boxing, Wrestling and Archery in a spectacular display of skill, determination and sporting excellence. Teenager Kumkum Mohod clinched gold in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin in a dramatic shoot-off. After the final was tied 5-5, Kumkum shot a perfect 10 against Oh’s 8, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal in the individual recurve event. Earlier, Kumkum defeated China’s Jingyi Zhu 6-2 in the semifinal to secure a quota place for India for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The quota is awarded to the country, and Kumkum became the first Indian recurve archer to assure herself of a medal in the women’s individual event. In hockey, Defending champions India will take on against Malaysia, with the two teams meeting at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium with eyes on the gold medal and an LA 2028 Olympics quota. Yesterday, Indian Women’s Hockey team clinched the gold medal, defeating defending champions China 1-nil in the closely fought final. Lalremsiami Hmarzote scored the decisive lone goal for India, while goalkeeper Savita Punia produced a crucial save from a penalty stroke to preserve the lead and secure the gold medal. The victory marks India’s first women hockey gold at the Asian Games in 44 years, ending a long wait for the title. The Women’s Hockey team has also secured a direct berth at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Earlier, Indian wrestler Sujeet Kalkal scripted a remarkable comeback to win the gold medal in the men’s 65-kilogram freestyle event. The 23-year-old Indian produced a stunning fightback in the final, recovering from a 4-9 deficit to defeat Tajikistan’s Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 and clinch the Asian Games title. With this victory, Sujeet has joined the elite company of Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, becoming the third Indian wrestler to win Asian Games gold in the men’s 65-kilogram category. In Boxing, Parveen Hooda won the gold medal in the women’s 65kg category, defeating Chinese Taipei’s Nien-Chin Chen 3-2 in a split decision in the final. Ankush Panghal clinched the gold medal in the men’s 80-kilogram category, defeating South Korea’s Kim Minseong by a split decision, 4-0, in the final. India’s star woman boxer Lovlina Borgohain also clinched a gold medal in the 75kg category, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final. It is India’s only second gold medal in women’s boxing at the Asian Games, following Mary Kom’s gold in 2014. In Archery, the women’s recurve team created history by clinching its maiden Asian Games gold medal. The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final. India also bagged silver in the mixed recurve team event. Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara finished runners-up after going down 3-5 to China in a closely contested final. In Sepaktakraw, India secured the bronze medal in the men’s quadrant event. The Indian team lost 0-2 to Japan in the semi-final but earned a place on the podium. In Sailing, Nethra Kumanan clinched bronze in the women’s dinghy event. The 29-year-old Indian sailor finished third with an overall score of 14 points. With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fifth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 77, including 17 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals.

national_raw_news.title: Officials of Doordarshan, PIB killed in Mizoram accident - Nagaland Post
national_raw_news.content: Officials of Doordarshan, PIB killed in Mizoram accident Facebook Instagram Linkedin RSS X Nagaland Northeast National World Infotainment NagaBuzz Sports Nagaland Sports Business Editorial Opinion Search Nagaland Post Search Nagaland Northeast National World Infotainment NagaBuzz Sports Nagaland Sports Business Editorial Opinion Nagaland Post Saturday, October 3, 2026 Nagaland Post Nagaland Post Search Nagaland Northeast National World Infotainment NagaBuzz Sports Nagaland Sports Business Editorial Opinion Nagaland Post Nagaland Northeast National World Infotainment NagaBuzz Sports Nagaland Sports Business Editorial Opinion Search Northeast Officials of Doordarshan, PIB killed in Mizoram accident Officials of Doordarshan, PIB killed in Mizoram accident October 3, 2026 Aizawl, Oct 2 (PTI): The bodies of Aizawl Doordarshan Director (News) Nampibou Marinmai and Press Information Bureau (PIB) Additional Director General Engam Pame will be sent to their respective hometowns in Manipur on Friday after autopsy, a PIB official said. Marinmai and Pame were among three central government officials killed when their car plunged into a deep gorge near Sataek village, about 30 km south of Aizawl, on Thursday. H Lianvela, a multi-tasking staff (MTS) member of the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) field office here, also died in the accident, while the driver, Gojendro Dey of CBC, Aizawl, sustained severe injuries and was admitted to Zoram Medical College and Hospital (ZMCH) at Falkawn near Aizawl, the official said. The four were returning to Aizawl after planting a tree at Sialsuk village in memory of Pame’s brother, who had died in an accident, when their vehicle veered off the road and plunged into the gorge after the driver suddenly experienced uneasiness and was unable to move his limbs or open his eyes, he said. The three bodies were brought to ZMCH on Thursday night for postmortem, which is scheduled to be conducted on Friday. The bodies of Marinmai and Pame will subsequently be sent to their native places in Manipur, the official said. Office-bearers of the Mizoram Journalists’ Association (MJA) also visited ZMCH on Thursday to offer condolences and pay homage to the three officials. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Lalduhoma, Mizo National Front (MNF) president Zoramthanga and Mizoram Congress unit president Lal Thanzara on Friday condoled the deaths. Lalduhoma described the deaths as tragic and untimely and expressed solidarity with the bereaved families and their loved ones. “Their sudden and untimely passing is a profound loss, and I share in the grief of all who mourn them,” the chief minister added. national_raw_news.title: INS Trishul arrives in Spain after Varuna exercise with French Navy as part ongoing deployment
national_raw_news.content: INS Trishul arrives in Spain after Varuna exercise with French Navy as part ongoing deployment Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर INS Trishul arrives in Spain after Varuna exercise with French Navy as part ongoing deployment ANI | Updated: Oct 03, 2026 06:45 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Valencia [ Spain ], October 3 (ANI): Indian Naval Ship (INS) Trishul, a frontline guided-missile stealth frigate of the Indian Navy, arrived at Valencia , Spain , as part of its ongoing deployment to the Mediterranean, Atlantic and adjoining maritime regions, the Ministry of Defence said on Friday. According to the ministry, the frigate arrived at Valencia on September 30, during which it will undertake professional interactions, cross-deck visits, sporting events and cultural engagements with the Spanish Navy. The engagements are aimed at facilitating the exchange of operational experiences and fostering greater mutual understanding between the two navies. The visit is part of the Indian Navy's sustained maritime engagement with friendly foreign countries and partner navies, aimed at strengthening professional ties and enhancing cooperation at sea. The deployment comes after INS Trishul participated in the 24th edition of Exercise Varuna, the annual bilateral maritime exercise between the Indian Navy and the French Navy, at Toulon, France. INS Trishul had arrived at Toulon on September 22 to participate in the exercise. The harbour phase included professional, sporting and cultural engagements between personnel of the two navies. During the Toulon visit, the Commanding Officer of INS Trishul called on Rear Admiral Mackara Ouk, Deputy Commander-in-Chief for Operations (CECMED), and interacted with senior leadership of the French Navy. The Commanding Officer, officers and crew of INS Trishul also laid a wreath at the Mazargues War Memorial in Marseille in remembrance of 205 Indian soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during the World Wars. As part of the professional engagements, personnel undertook cross-deck visits and exchanged operational experiences. The ship's crew also visited French Navy vessels Charles de Gaulle, Forbin and La Fayette, gaining insights into carrier operations, aviation facilities and practices onboard the vessels. INS Trishul also hosted a cultural interaction onboard, attended by Vice Admiral (Retd) Laurent Isnard, Deputy Mayor of Toulon, French Navy officers and civil dignitaries. A friendly volleyball match between personnel of the two navies further fostered camaraderie. The sea phase of Exercise Varuna saw INS Trishul operate alongside French Navy units, including FDA Forbin, FLF La Fayette and SNA Suffren, as well as NH90 helicopters and Atlantique 2 maritime patrol aircraft. The exercise featured anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare drills, live-firing exercises and cross-deck helicopter landing serials, aimed at enhancing operational coordination, interoperability and synergy between the two navies. The Indian Navy's deployment across the Mediterranean, Atlantic and adjoining maritime regions underscores its focus on operational readiness, maritime engagement and international outreach. The ongoing deployment and port call in Valencia are expected to further strengthen India's maritime engagement with partner navies and contribute to a secure and stable maritime environment, the Ministry of Defence said. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) reviewed enforcement actions, inspections and compliance status across the National Capital Region (NCR) for the reporting period from September 8 to September 24, with 197 inspections conducted during the 17-day period, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change said on Friday. The 140th meeting of the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) of CAQM was held on October 1 to review the enforcement status. During the 17-day reporting period, a total of 197 inspections were reported, comprising 10 inspections at Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites, 111 inspections in the Industrial Sector and 76 inspections related to Diesel Generator (DG) sets. The industrial sector inspections included 22 inspections conducted as part of a special inspection drive. Based on the inspections, violations were reported in 85 cases, comprising 8 C&D cases, 49 industrial cases and 28 DG-related cases. As per the violations reported by the concerned sectors, various enforcement actions have been proposed. These include closure of 4 C&D projects and 1 industrial unit; sealing of 28 DG sets; issuance of orders/directions for compliance in 17 cases, including 4 DG sets; and Environmental Compensation (EC) in 10 cases. Other proposed actions include issuance of letters to project proponents, re-inspection, forwarding of cases to CPCB/SPCB, advisories and other appropriate follow-up measures. The ETF was apprised of the action taken during the special inspection drive conducted in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh on September 15 by 7 teams of the Flying Squads of the Commission, along with District Administration and Police personnel and officers of UPPCB. A total of 22 premises were inspected, of which 05 were found compliant and 1 had already been sealed by UPPCB. The actions suggested in the remaining cases include closure of 4 units, sealing of 1 DG set, issuance of orders in 5 cases, imposition of EC in 4 cases, and re-inspection and prosecution in 2 cases, the Ministry said. The status of resumption orders issued after the previous ETF meeting was also reviewed. As of September 30, a total of 9 resumption orders had been issued, comprising 2 industrial units and 7 C&D sites. national_raw_news.title: Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief ...
national_raw_news.content: Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief over tragic deaths - The Sangai Express - Largest Circulated NewsPaper in Manipur Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief over tragic deaths 02-Oct-2026 | IMPHAL, Oct 2 (PIB) The Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Imphal, have expressed profound grief over the tragic demise of Dr Engam Pame, Additional Director General, PIB & CBC Regional Office, Imphal; Nampibou Marinmai, Director (News), DDK and All India Radio (AIR), Aizawl, and H Lianvela, Multi-Tasking Staff member, CBC, Aizawl, who lost their lives in a tragic road accident near Sateek in Mizoram on Thursday. Dr Engam Pame was a senior Indian Information Service (IIS) officer serving as Additional Director General, PIB & CBC Regional Office, Imphal. He joined the PIB/CBC Regional Office, Imphal, on July 29, 2022, as Regional Director. During his distinguished career, he had also served as Director, Directorate of Field Publicity, Shillong, and had been associated with the Regional News Unit of Doordarshan Kendra, Imphal. He was the Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC), Manipur Chapter, it said. Born on November 30, 1967, Dr Pame made significant contributions to public communication and information dissemination, it added. During his tenure at PIB and CBC, Imphal, he played an important role in strengthening coordination between the Government and the media fraternity and in facilitating the dissemination of information on government Golicies, programmes and initiatives, it said. The statement continued that Nampibou Marinmai was also an IIS officer and was serving as Director (News), DDK and AIR, Aizawl. He was Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC) and had earlier served as Public Relations Officer with the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. During his tenure with the Ministry of Defence, he was associated with defence-related public relations, media reporting and communication. Through his long association with news and public broadcasting, the PIB said that Marinmai made valuable contributions to public communication and information dissemination. Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw expressed deep sorrow over the demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai and H Lianvela and conveyed his heartfelt condolences to their bereaved families, friends and colleagues. Several senior officials of the Ministry and its attached organisations also expressed deep sorrow over the tragic loss and conveyed their heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. They expressed solidarity with the families, friends and colleagues of the departed during this hour of immense grief. The Ministry of Defence also mourned the demise of Nampibou Marinmai, recalling his services as Public Relations Officer (Defence) and his long-standing association with defence reporting. Officials and staff of PIB, CBC and Akashvani, Imphal, observed a two-minute silence in memory of the departed souls and expressed their deepest condolences to the bereaved families. They also prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured driver and extended their support and solidarity to those affected by the tragedy....
